chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Muyassar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I order a slave girl to wash my garment from semen, but she does not wash it thoroughly, so I pray in it when it is dry.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Repeat your prayer. Indeed, if you had washed it yourself, there would be no blame upon you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if one's clothes are washed by someone else but not thoroughly cleaned from semen?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'ease in worship' (al-taysir), distinguishing between the strict liability of the owner for a servant's negligence and the personal exemption granted when one performs the act of purification oneself. It underscores the theological emphasis on individual agency and divine mercy, suggesting that the intent and direct effort of the worshipper mitigate the ritual impurity (najāsah) more leniently than the mechanical action of another.
